name: Vorpal Hare
description: A white hare with a fixed, glassy stare and teeth like a surgeon's shears. The Dark Lord's flesh crafters bred them either as a terror weapon or as a joke, and nobody who has met one has been able to say which; most suspect both. It knows no fear, it does not stop, and it goes for the throat.

name: Grave Wyrm
description: A dragon that would not die, its hide long since sloughed from a cage of black bone. It breathes a fog of grave-cold that rots what it does not freeze, and its claws leave the living rigid as corpses. Grave wyrms remember every hoard they ever lost.

name: Gnawing Dead
description: A corpse that rose hungry. It is quick where other dead are slow, all nails and teeth, and it goes for the soft parts. Those it bites sicken, and those who die of the sickness do not stay down.

name: Colossus Bear
description: Some cubs never stop growing. A colossus bear stands as tall as a watchtower on its hind legs and is hungry every waking hour; whole valleys empty of game when one wakes from its winter sleep.

name: Giant Ant
description: An ant the size of a pony, red or black, in a chitin shell that turns blades. Shy at first sight, relentless once the fight starts. Their tunnels sometimes run through veins of raw gold, which they hoard for the shine.

name: Cave Bear
description: A shaggy brute bigger than any common bear, that kills anything its own size or smaller and drags it back to the dark. It crushes what it cannot bite.

name: Chimera
description: Lion, goat, and dragon on one winged body: a crafter's showpiece from the old war that learned to breed. All three heads hate each other and everything else, and the dragon head breathes fire.

name: Gnoll
description: Hyena-headed raiders who hunt in loose packs by night and see in the dark. Stronger than they look and crueler than they need to be, they follow whoever is biggest, and break when the biggest falls.

name: Hill Giant
description: Twelve feet of hide-wrapped muscle with a tree-trunk club and a short temper. Hill giants raid farms, bully ogres into service, and keep dire wolves as dogs.

name: Manticore
description: A winged lion with a man's ruined face and a tail of iron spikes it flings like javelins. It wears prey down from the air before it lands to feed, and it prefers people.

name: Giant Scorpion
description: A scorpion the size of a donkey that attacks whatever it sees. Its claws pin, and its sting carries a venom that eats the strength out of the strongest.

name: Giant Rattlesnake
description: Twenty feet of diamond-backed snake whose rattle is the last warning anyone gets. Its venom swells the limb and burns for days.

name: Giant Black Widow
description: A glossy black spider a yard across with a red hourglass on its belly. It strings near-invisible webs across passages and waits; its venom is among the deadliest in the Dark Lands.

name: Unicorn
description: A white horse-shaped thing with a spiral horn that cuts like an enchanted blade. Shy and proud, it fights only for itself or its wood, and its horn's touch is said to close wounds.

name: Alicorn
description: A unicorn in every line save its burning red eyes and the fangs behind its lips. Where a unicorn defends, an alicorn hunts.

name: Vampire
description: A noble corpse that drinks the living. It casts no shadow and shows no reflection, its gaze bends the will, and every drop it drinks knits its wounds. Those it drains to death rise as its slaves.

name: Zombie
description: A corpse on its feet and nothing behind its eyes. Slow and silent, it shrugs off clubs and arrows and has to be hacked apart before it stops.

name: Raised Zombie
description: A corpse raised by Raise Corpse (vendor/wwn-srd 4.6.0), flesh still on its bones. It obeys its necromancer with a human degree of understanding and no will of its own, and blunt blows sink into it.

name: Raised Skeleton
description: A corpse raised by Raise Corpse and stripped to the bone: a little harder to hit, and blades find little to cut. It obeys its necromancer without question.

name: Grave Knight
description: A powerful corpse raised by Raise Grave Knight (vendor/wwn-srd 4.6.0): fully intelligent, utterly devoted to its creator, and whole again at every dusk.

name: Mushroom Sporeling
description: A knee-high mushroom on stubby root-legs, its cap still damp from the dark where it sprouted. Sporelings shamble about the deep places in mobs, clubbing at anything warm and planting their dead to feed the next crop.

name: Mushroom Warrior
description: A man-sized fungus with a cap gone hard and woody as a shield-boss. Warriors guard the spore beds of their colony and swing knotted stalks like clubs; they make no sound but a wet creak.

name: Mushroom Spore Shaman
description: An old, pale fungus hung with dangling gills. It speaks to its colony in clouds of scent, and its lashing tendrils burst into spores that lock a victim's limbs.

name: Mushroom King
description: The ancient heart of a fungal colony, a towering bulk of shelf-caps and pallid flesh that has fed for centuries on whatever died in the dark. The whole colony moves at its will.

name: Walking Tree
description: An old tree that has pulled its roots from the ground and remembers how to walk. Walking trees are slow and patient and hate the axe; they crush what they catch with limbs like battering rams.

name: Swamp Thing
description: A heap of rotting reeds, moss, and black mud that rises from the mire in the shape of a man. Blows sink into it without effect, and it drags its prey down into the water to feed the bog.

name: Wood Golem
description: A guardian carved from heartwood and bound with old sorcery, its joints pegged and its face a blank of grain. It does not tire or sleep, and it does what it was made to do until it is splintered.

name: Phantasmal Eidolon
description: A half-real servant called up by Calculation of the Phantasmal Eidolon, in whatever shape its caster wished. It obeys with fearless devotion until dawn, and its blows only knock foes senseless.

name: Walking Sapling
description: A young tree that has learned to walk before it learned patience. Saplings wander the forest edges alone, lashing at travelers with whip-thin limbs, and will one day root and grow into something far worse.
